report.tagline: A social app for runners, cyclists and other athletes to record workouts, share them with friends and compete on routes, with a paid subscription for deeper features.
report.simpleSummary: Strava is like Instagram for exercise. You record a run or ride with your phone or watch, and it shows up in your friends' feeds with a map, distance and pace. Friends give 'kudos' (likes) and comments, and you can race others on popular stretches of road called segments. The basic app is free; a subscription of about $80 a year adds training plans, route planning and detailed analysis. It has about 195 million registered users and filed to go public in early 2026.

overview.whatItDoes: Strava records workouts using GPS from a phone or a connected device like Garmin, Apple Watch or Wahoo, and turns each one into a shareable post. It adds social features such as followers, kudos, clubs and challenges, and competitive features like segment leaderboards. Subscribers get route building, training plans, progress analysis and safety tools. Strava bought Runna, a running coaching app, and The Breakaway, a cycling training app, in 2025.
howItWorks: A user signs up free and connects a watch or uses the phone app to record an activity.
After a run or ride, the activity uploads to Strava with a map, stats and photos.
Followers see it in their feed and give kudos or comments.
Segments, which are user-made stretches of road or trail, have leaderboards; the fastest gets KOM or QOM (King or Queen of the Mountain).
Clubs and monthly challenges bring groups together, often sponsored by brands.
A subscription unlocks features like route builder, Beacon safety sharing, training plans and detailed segment results.
overview.valueProposition: Make every workout count: record it, share it with people who care, see your progress and get a bit of friendly competition, all in one place, whatever device you use.

businessModel.summary: Strava is free to use, and makes most of its money from about 2% of users who pay for a subscription. Smaller revenue comes from brands that sponsor challenges and from partnerships.

revenueStreams.detail: Individual, student, family and Runna bundle plans; the large majority of revenue.
Brands like sportswear companies pay to run challenges and clubs.
Anonymised activity data shared with city planners, historically free or low-cost.

businessModel.pricing: Free basic app. Subscription $79.99 a year or $11.99 a month in the US; family $139.99 a year; student $39.99 a year; Strava + Runna $149.99 a year. Prices differ by country.
costDrivers: Cloud hosting for maps and activity data
App store fees on in-app subscriptions
businessModel.unitEconomics: A subscriber paying $79.99 a year gives Strava about $56 to $68 after app store fees, or close to $80 if they paid on the web. Serving a user costs a few dollars a year in hosting. The 98% of users who do not pay still cost money but create the social feed and data that make the paid features useful. Because most new users arrive through friends, CAC is low, so each subscriber who renews is very profitable.

howTheyGetUsers: Friends and run clubs inviting each other
Activities shared to Instagram and other social apps
Brand challenges and events like big city marathons
Gen Z run club boom since 2024
whatBringsUsersBack: Kudos and comments after every workout
growth.moat: Strava has a strong network effect: your friends, clubs and history are already there. Its segments and heatmaps come from billions of activities that a new app cannot recreate. Being device-neutral also makes it the place where everyone's data meets, which Garmin or Apple cannot easily offer.

competitors.name: Garmin Connect
competitors.positioning: Free app for Garmin device owners with deep training data.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Garmin is tied to its own devices; Strava is social and works with all devices.

competitors.name: Apple Fitness and Apple Health
competitors.positioning: Built into iPhone and Apple Watch.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Apple has distribution but a weaker social layer and no segments.

competitors.name: Nike Run Club and adidas Running
competitors.positioning: Free running apps from sportswear brands.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Free and guided, but less community and cycling support.

competitors.name: Komoot
competitors.positioning: Route planning for hiking and cycling.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Better for planning trips; Strava is stronger for social and competition.

northStar.metric: Weekly active athletes who upload at least one activity and receive or give kudos
northStar.why: An upload with social interaction is the moment Strava delivers its core value: motivation through community. It predicts both retention and conversion to paid.

improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More trust and engagement on segments.

improvementIdeas.idea: Show free users one personalised insight a week with a teaser of the paid version

pmLessons: Social features can turn a utility (tracking) into a habit. Kudos is a tiny feature with a huge effect.
Freemium works when free users create value for paying users, like the data behind routes and heatmaps.
Be careful when moving features behind a paywall; loyal users notice and complain loudly.
Being neutral across devices can be a moat when everyone else is building a closed system.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase Strava's paid conversion from 2%?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment users by sport and goal, find the moment of need (race training), design trials around it, measure trial to paid.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature for Gen Z run clubs on Strava.
interviewQuestions.hint: Understand club organisers' jobs, propose tools, define a club activity metric.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Strava's north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weekly active athletes uploading with social interaction; explain why not just sign-ups or revenue.

interviewQuestions.question: Garmin starts adding a social feed. How should Strava respond?
interviewQuestions.hint: Lean into device neutrality, network effects and community; avoid conflict that hurts users.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure the success of the Runna acquisition?
interviewQuestions.hint: Bundle uptake, subscriber retention of bundle users vs others, revenue per user.
